title: From Knowledge to innovation capabilities
text: To ensure full reproducibility and streamline execution time, we load the curated longitudinal dataset generated by the VIRTECOM NetLogo simulation (data.RData), encompassing 1,440,720 simulation records across 720 independent runs (\(t \in [1, 2000]\)). We then extract the terminal cross-sectional snapshot at \(t = 2000\) (df_ss) representing quasi-stationary steady-state outcomes.

title: From Knowledge to innovation capabilities
text:

2.1.2 Temporal Evolution of Collective Know‑How

p_ck_time <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(step, max.triads.per.worker) %>%
  summarise(
    CK = mean(mean.firm.ck),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      step,
      CK,
      color = factor(max.triads.per.worker)
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .9) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulation Step",
    y = "Mean Collective Know-How",
    color = "MT"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_ck_time










2.1.3 Collective Know‑How Heatmap

p_ck_heatmap <- df_ss %>%
  group_by(
    max.triads.per.worker,
    credit.limit.base
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    CK = mean(mean.firm.ck),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      factor(max.triads.per.worker),
      factor(credit.limit.base),
      fill = CK
    )
  ) +
  geom_tile(color="white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    x = "Max Triads",
    y = "Credit Limit",
    fill = "CK"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_ck_heatmap

2.1.5 Interpretation
The results indicate that collective know‑how emerges primarily from cognitive coordination structures. Cognitive constraints explain nearly all observed variation in collective know‑how, whereas access to credit has negligible explanatory power.
